messages:
Sophie Lane: FYI customer on Private (us-east) seeing intermittent 400s + a bunch of TLS handshake errors in our control-plane logs. They only go through the DX/private peering. Happening ~every 5-10m, lasts a minute. No recent deploys.

Raj Patel: Can you paste the exact log lines? Also which client is hitting them (internal ALB, customer LB, direct)?

Sophie Lane: Logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:41Z control-plane error: tls handshake failed: remote error: handshake failure; conn_id=xyz
2026-03-15T09:12:41Z proxy warn: upstream returned 400 for request id abc123
2026-03-15T09:12:52Z control-plane info: connection reset by peer during TLS handshake
```
Requests come from customer's VPC over Direct Connect -> our VPC peering. They run mutual-TLS for some endpoints. Customer says their app gets 502/400 and retries.

Maria Gomez: Can you ask them to run a quick repro from their side and share outputs? Useful commands:
```
curl -v --key client.key --cert client.crt https://private-api.internal/health
openssl s_client -connect private-api.internal:443 -status -showcerts
dig @<their-resolver> ocsp.example-ca.com +short
traceroute -n private-api.internal
tcpdump -i any host ocsp.example-ca.com or port 80 or port 53
```
If openssl -status shows no OCSP response and tcpdump shows no outgoing to the OCSP responder, that suggests egress/DNS issue.

Sophie Lane: Customer ran s_client and got: "OCSP response: no response sent" and curl shows: "SSL: certificate verification failed" intermittently. They also attached a tcpdump snippet — no packets to ocsp.* hosts, only to their internal resolver.

Chris Wu: This smells like egress allowlist / split-horizon DNS. If their resolver doesn't forward queries to internet OCSP responders (or the peering path blocks egress), TLS clients that expect OCSP stapling/validation can fail. With mutual TLS, missing OCSP for intermediate CA sometimes causes handshake to abort depending on client settings.

Raj Patel: Checklist for customer to verify:
- Ensure their on-prem firewall/NAT allows outbound TCP/UDP 53 to the DNS forwarder and outbound TCP/443 (or 80) to well-known OCSP/CRL endpoints for the CA that signed the server cert.
- Confirm NACLs / security groups on the VPC and peering route tables do not block return traffic.
- Check MTU/path MTU if they're encapsulating (DX + customer CPE sometimes needs clamping).

Maria Gomez: Quick repro commands I want from them (single paste):
```
# DNS
dig @<their-resolver> ocsp.example-ca.com +short
dig +trace ocsp.example-ca.com
# OCSP
openssl s_client -connect private-api.internal:443 -status -servername private-api.internal
# capture
sudo tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/ocsp.pcap host ocsp.example-ca.com or port 80 or port 53
```
If dig +trace returns IPs but tcpdump doesn't show any egress, the forwarder is dropping/blackholing.

Sophie Lane: They ran dig +trace — it stalls at their internal resolver. They confirmed corporate firewall only allows a small egress allowlist (strict). They said they didn't have OCSP domains whitelisted.

Alex Chen: Product note: our Private control plane occasionally performs OCSP checks at connection time (transitive dependencies + some CA chains we use). We should document OCSP/CRL endpoints customers must allow for Private deployments.

Raj Patel: Temporary workaround we validated with customer: add outbound allowlist entries to their edge firewall for the OCSP responder hosts (TCP 80/443 depending on CA) and allow DNS forwarder to resolve to public. After they whitelisted ocsp.digicert.com and ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org, the TLS errors stopped.

Chris Wu: Also verify the peering path allows ephemeral outbound ephemeral ports back to the client. If the customer's NAT is source-rewriting in an unexpected way, TCP handshakes to OCSP may fail.

Sophie Lane: Customer confirmed: after whitelisting the OCSP hosts + allowing DNS forward to 8.8.8.8 (for test), errors disappeared for 24h. They rolled the change to prod now.

Raj Patel: Long-term action items:
- Eng-infra to add an entry in Private deployment runbook listing required outbound domains/ports (OCSP, CRL, time servers, KMS endpoints if using cloud KMS).
- Update onboarding checklist for Dedicated/Private customers to include egress policy template.
- We should also add a healthcheck that fails with a clear message when OCSP lookups fail (avoid confusing 400/handshake errors).

Alex Chen: Filed doc ticket and will add to onboarding templates.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-2026-45 created (severity: low) — "Private peering: OCSP/DNS egress allowlist caused intermittent TLS handshake failures"

Sophie Lane: Closing note: customer happy, rollback not needed. Will follow up next week to verify no regressions. :white_check_mark:
